title: "Mendelian Randomization Feasibility: Endometriosis and Substance Addiction"
author: "Ellen Martin"
date: "2026-09-03"
output: html_document
---

SUMMARY:
- overall, some evidence of shared genetic architecture (in negative direction)
- but no evidence of causal associations between endometriosis and addiction-rf.

### Reading Opiod Use Disorder (Deak et al., 2022)

```{r}
opioid_raw <- fread("/gpfs/gibbs/project/polimanti/ejm96/project/data/OUD_EUR_Sumstats_Deak2022.gz", header = T) 
opioid_sumstats <- opioid_raw
head(opioid_sumstats) #checking headers

colnames(opioid_sumstats)

opioid_effect <- fread("/gpfs/gibbs/project/polimanti/ejm96/project/data/OUD_EUR_Sumstats_Deak2022_betase.gz", header = T) 
head(opioid_effect)

#getting rsid based on chr and pos
opioid_effect <- as.data.table(opioid_effect)
opioid_sumstats <- as.data.table(opioid_sumstats)

opioid_effect[, c("chr", "bp") := tstrsplit(SNP, ":", fixed = TRUE)]

opioid_effect[, chr := as.integer(chr)]
opioid_effect[, bp  := as.integer(bp)]

#merging
opioid_sumstats <- merge(
    opioid_sumstats,
    opioid_effect[, .(
        chr,
        bp,
        A1_effect = A1,
        A2_effect = A2,
        Z_effect = Z,
        P_effect = P,
        N,
        SE,
        Beta
    )],
    by = c("chr", "bp")
)

# Standardize allele case
opioid_sumstats[, `:=`(
    a1 = toupper(a1),
    a2 = toupper(a2),
    A1_effect = toupper(A1_effect),
    A2_effect = toupper(A2_effect)
)]


```

### QC pipeline
```{r endometriosis quality control, eval=FALSE}



endo_qc <- as.data.table(endo_sumstats)[
  chr %between% c(1L, 22L) &
  pos > 0 &
  EA %chin% c("A", "C", "G", "T") &
  OA %chin% c("A", "C", "G", "T") &
  EA != OA &
  is.finite(beta) &
  is.finite(se) &
  se > 0 &
  is.finite(pval) &
  pval > 0 &
  pval <= 1 &
  is.finite(eaf) &
  eaf > 0 &
  eaf < 1
]

#endo_qc[, SNP := paste(chr, pos, sep = ":")]

#endo_qc <- unique(endo_qc, by = "SNP") #deduplicates by SNP (new column made by combing chr and pos)

head(endo_qc)
```

# Mendelian Randomization
### Endometriosis to Substance
- from endometriosis (GWAS sig) --> substance dependence rf (Hatoum et al)
- overall finds no evidence of causal association from endo --> addiction
- The five independent endometriosis instruments showed no evidence of a causal association with substance addiction/dependence using IVW (β = −0.0081, 95% CI −0.0295 to 0.0134, P = 0.462). Estimates from MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, and bootstrap MR-Egger were consistent with the IVW estimate. There was no evidence of heterogeneity (Cochran's Q = 0.56, P = 0.967) or directional horizontal pleiotropy (MR-Egger intercept = −0.00034, P = 0.924)


1) Overall MR + IVW with CI
- n.s.

```{r endo to substance MR}
Results_endo_to_substance <- run_mr_pipeline(
  clumped_dat = endo_to_substance_clumped,
  analysis_name = "Endometriosis → Substance (GWS)"
)

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(Results_endo_to_substance$mr),
  "markdown"
)

ivw <- subset(
  Results_endo_to_substance$mr,
  method == "Inverse variance weighted"
)

ivw$ci_lower <- ivw$b - 1.96 * ivw$se
ivw$ci_upper <- ivw$b + 1.96 * ivw$se

ivw[, c("b", "se", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "pval")]
```




2) Heterogeneity, Pleiotropy and Egger
- No evidence of heterogeneity, pleiotropy or outlier SNPs

## MR PRESSO and LeaveOneOut
- since we have evidence of heterogeneity we can use MR PRESSO to identify SNPs acting in the disagreeing direction, and potentially remove, then check if an effect exists
- but note this is still the relaxed threshold

### LeaveOneOut Endo to Substance
- no significant outliers detected

```{r presso endo to substance}
library(MRPRESSO)

mr_presso_result <- mr_presso(
  BetaOutcome = "beta.outcome",
  BetaExposure = "beta.exposure",
  SdOutcome = "se.outcome",
  SdExposure = "se.exposure",
  OUTLIERtest = TRUE,
  DISTORTIONtest = TRUE,
  data = as.data.frame(endo_to_substance_relaxed_clumped),
  NbDistribution = 1500,
  SignifThreshold = 0.05
)

mr_presso_result

```

### LeaveOneOut and PRESSO substance to endo

```{r}

mr_presso_result <- mr_presso(
  BetaOutcome = "beta.outcome",
  BetaExposure = "beta.exposure",
  SdOutcome = "se.outcome",
  SdExposure = "se.exposure",
  OUTLIERtest = TRUE,
  DISTORTIONtest = TRUE,
  data = as.data.frame(substance_to_endo_relaxed_clumped),
  NbDistribution = 1500,
  SignifThreshold = 0.05
)

mr_presso_result

# outliers
mr_presso_result$`MR-PRESSO results`$`Outlier Test`

data.frame(
  row = rownames(substance_to_endo_relaxed_clumped),
  SNP = substance_to_endo_relaxed_clumped$SNP
)

substance_to_endo_relaxed_clumped[18, ]
```
- the p-value of the global MR-PRESSO is 0.009, indicating directional horizontal pleitoropy, and is consistent with the results of Cochran's Q. 
- The relaxed substance → endometriosis analysis demonstrates significant between-instrument heterogeneity, with MR-PRESSO identifying one outlying variant. However, there was no significant distortion of the causal estimate after accounting for the outlier, and the overall IVW estimate remained null.

### Removing Outlier for MR

```{r mr presso outlier}
substance_to_endo_no_outlier <- substance_to_endo_relaxed_clumped[
  substance_to_endo_relaxed_clumped$SNP != "rs293553",
]

#Confirm N SNPs remain
nrow(substance_to_endo_no_outlier)

Results_substance_to_endo_no_outlier <- run_mr_pipeline(
  clumped_dat = substance_to_endo_no_outlier,
  analysis_name = "Substance → Endometriosis (Relaxed + Outlier Removed)"
)

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(Results_substance_to_endo_no_outlier$mr),
  "markdown"
)

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(Results_substance_to_endo_no_outlier$heterogeneity),
  "markdown"
)

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(Results_substance_to_endo_no_outlier$pleiotropy),
  "markdown"
)


```
-In the relaxed-threshold analysis of substance addiction/dependence on endometriosis, significant heterogeneity was initially observed across the 27 genetic instruments (Cochran's Q P = 0.006). MR-PRESSO identified  as a significant outlier (P = 0.018). Following exclusion of rs293553, there was no longer evidence of heterogeneity. The IVW estimate remained null. Consistent with the MR-PRESSO distortion test (P = 0.125), exclusion of the outlier did not provide evidence of an altered causal estimate. These findings support the robustness of the null association to the identified outlier.

```{r computing N, eval=FALSE}
# Keep SNPs with valid MAF and SE
hatoum_N_dat <- hatoum_freq[
  !is.na(MAF) &
  !is.na(se) &
  MAF > 0 &
  MAF < 0.5
]

# Genomic SEM effective N estimate
hatoum_N_dat[, N_hat := 1 / (
  2 * MAF * (1 - MAF) * se^2
)]

# Genomic SEM recommendation: use common variants (MAF >= 0.10)
hatoum_N_common <- hatoum_N_dat[MAF >= 0.10]

N_hat <- mean(hatoum_N_common$N_hat, na.rm = TRUE)

N_hat
```

```{r checking Neff, eval=FALSE}
c(
  total_snps = nrow(hatoum),
  snps_with_maf = nrow(hatoum_N_dat),
  snps_maf_ge_0.10 = nrow(hatoum_N_common),
  N_hat = N_hat
)

summary(hatoum_N_common$N_hat)
quantile(
  hatoum_N_common$N_hat,
  probs = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95, 0.99),
  na.rm = TRUE
)
```

### Endometriosis Addiction RF LDSC


```{r genetic correlation endo and addiction rf}
endo_munged <- "/gpfs/gibbs/project/polimanti/ejm96/project/data/finngen_endometriosis_ldsc.sumstats.gz"

hatoum_munged <- "/gpfs/gibbs/project/polimanti/ejm96/project/data/substance_addiction_rf_ldsc.sumstats.gz"

eur_ld <- "/gpfs/gibbs/pi/polimanti/LDSC_files/eur_w_ld_chr/"

rg_out <- "/gpfs/gibbs/project/polimanti/ejm96/project/data/endometriosis_addiction_rf_rg"

system2(
  ldsc_python,
  args = c(
    file.path(cb_ldsc_dir, "ldsc.py"),
    "--rg",
    paste(endo_munged, hatoum_munged, sep = ","),
    "--ref-ld-chr", eur_ld,
    "--w-ld-chr", eur_ld,
    "--out", rg_out
  )
)
```
Cross-trait LD score regression identified a modest negative genetic correlation between endometriosis and the multivariate addiction risk factor (\(r_g=-0.096\), SE = 0.037, \(P=0.009\)), based on 636,518 SNPs with valid alleles. The cross-trait LDSC intercept was consistent with zero (−0.004, SE = 0.007), suggesting little evidence of bias due to correlated confounding or sample overlap

Endometriosis and addiction liability appear to share some genetic architecture, with effects tending to be oppositely directed, but the current analyses do not support a causal relationship between the two phenotypes.

```{r genetic correlation endo and tobacco}
    "--w-ld-chr", eur_ld,
    "--out", rg_out
  )
)
```
| Phenotype    |     \(r_g\) |     SE |          P |
| ------------ | ----------: | -----: | ---------: |
| Addiction-rf |     −0.0958 | 0.0367 |     0.0090 |
| PAU          |     −0.0417 | 0.0274 |     0.1288 |
| CUD          |     −0.1297 | 0.0545 |     0.0173 |
| OUD          | **−0.2043** | 0.0637 | **0.0013** |
| PTU/tobacco  | **−0.1673** | 0.0457 | **0.0002** |


- so it appears that the negative genetic association between endometriosis and addiction-rf is driven more-so by OUD and PTU/tobacco, which would survive multiple testing.
